chunks: Blessed is he who humbles himself, whose livelihood is pure, whose inner self is sound, whose character is virtuous, who spends his surplus wealth, who restrains his tongue from excess, who keeps his evil away from people, who is encompassed by the Sunnah, and who is not attributed to innovation.
ai.seo_question: What are the key virtues of a blessed person according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) delineates the comprehensive profile of the blessed, linking inner spiritual states—such as self-humility (tadhallul) and sincerity (sira) to outward ethical conduct like lawful earnings (khasb) and charitable spending. This synthesis reflects the Shia emphasis on the unity of belief and action, where adherence to the Prophetic Sunnah serves as the safeguard against religious innovation (bid'ah), ensuring both personal purity and communal orthodoxy.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Blessed be he who humbles himself, whose livelihood is pure, whose heart is chaste, whose habits are virtuous, who spends his savings (in the name of Allāh), who prevents his tongue from speaking nonsense, who keeps people safe from evil, who is pleased with the (Prophet’s) sunnah, and who is unconnected with innovation (in religion).
